notes: X-1, first leaf of the titled « Liste des courbes elliptiques à multiplication complexe dont l’invariant modulaire j est rationnel ». It lists imaginary quadratic fields, allowable conductors for class-number-one orders, and the use of Weber’s functions to compute j. Two entries are given: 1.1. has j(i)=2^6 3^3 and automorphism order 4; 1.2 has j(2i)=(2.3.11)^3. The displayed products evaluate to 1728 and 287496; this arithmetic does not verify the CM identities. The stated conductor lists contain 13 known (d,f) pairs, with an extra hypothetical d_? retained. The source explicitly says « plus peut-être une autre valeur d_? » and « (s’il existe) »; no later classification is substituted. The reader’s note « les d sont premiers ! » is false if applied to every displayed d, because 1 occurs. The note is preserved unchanged. The overbrace covers the first five d values; its quoted label remains doubtful only at its final s. H’s only independently set source text here is the marginal NB note; its surrounding notes are editorial descriptions and are not collated as omitted typescript. No date appears on this leaf.

checks.type: refuted, with the refined statement’s id
checks.outcome: The unqualified note « les d sont premiers ! » includes displayed d=1, which is not prime. Refined statement S080-NB-PRIMES-EXCEPT-1 is not asserted by the transcription and was not needed for the counterexample.
Direct integer arithmetic: 2^6*3^3=1728; (2*3*11)^3=66^3=287496. Only the products were checked, not their identification with j-values.

The displayed conductor counts are 2 for d=1, 3 for d=3, 2 for d=7, and 1 for each of six other displayed d: 2+3+2+6=13, excluding d_?. This is a count of the written list, not a proof of completeness.

legibility: Typescript and mathematical indices are very clear. The only substantial remaining reading doubt is the ending of the small handwritten brace label. C agrees with the visible body, including the joined lesrelations. H has only the marginal NB note as source transcription; its wording agrees, but its underline is missing.
